title: Waldorf Salad
subtitle: Apple, celery, walnut, and mayonnaise on crisp lettuce
excerpt: Eating apple, celery, toasted walnuts, and grapes dressed in a light lemon mayonnaise and served on butter lettuce leaves. A classic American hotel salad that translates perfectly to a light British lunch.

recipe.sourceNotes: The Waldorf salad was created in 1896 by Oscar Tschirky, maître d' of the Waldorf Hotel in New York. The original recipe contained only apples, celery, and mayonnaise; walnuts were added later and became a standard part of the dish. The lemon juice in the dressing prevents the apple from browning. Use a crisp eating apple (Granny Smith or Cox) rather than a sweet dessert apple.

content.text: Toss the apple in lemon juice immediately after cutting to prevent browning. Toast the walnuts briefly in a dry pan to bring out their flavour: raw walnuts taste bitter by comparison. Do not dress the salad more than 30 minutes before serving or the apple will soften.

items.preparation: cored, cut into small dice, tossed in lemon juice
butter lettuce, leaves separated, to serve

content.text: Toast the walnut pieces in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until lightly golden and fragrant. Remove from the heat and leave to cool.
Whisk the mayonnaise, crème fraîche, half the lemon juice, salt, and pepper together in a large bowl.
Add the apple (tossed in the remaining lemon juice), celery, grapes, and toasted walnuts to the bowl. Toss gently to coat everything in the dressing.
Arrange the lettuce leaves on a platter or individual plates. Spoon the Waldorf mixture over the top. Serve immediately.
